```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
ri <- function(x) knitr::inline_expr(x)
workdir <- file.path(tempdir(), "units-article")
dir.create(workdir, showWarnings = FALSE)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = workdir)
```

This article is for authors whose numbers have units, and for projects that
fix some values by choice: a trigger level, a reporting year, the name of a
study area. After it you will be able to print a number with its unit in the
right form, convert it as you print it, give weft the names of your own
units, and keep a project's chosen values in one dictionary file that every
document and pipeline reads.

```{r}
library(weft)
```

## Quantities

A **quantity** is a number with a unit. `u()` makes one. The unit is written
as it is, never evaluated as R, or as a string:

```{r}
u(35, m)
u(5, mg/L)
u(150, "CFU/100 mL")
```

`u()` is a short form of `units::set_units()`, and all arithmetic is the
units package's. Units combine, cancel and convert, and adding two units
that do not convert is an error:

```{r, error = TRUE}
u(3, m) + u(20, cm)
u(3, m) / u(50, cm)
u(3, m) + u(2, kg)
```

A quantity cannot be compared with a bare number. A check states its unit:

```{r, error = TRUE}
claim(u(3, m), . > 2)
claim(u(3, m), . > u(2, m))
```

## Printing a quantity

A formatter prints the unit after the number, separated by a no-break space.
You do not type the unit in the prose.

```{r}
fmt_num(u(35, m))
fmt_num(u(1.2, m^2))
fmt_num(u(20, degC))
fmt_num(u(35, "%"))
fmt_num(u(7.2, pH))
```

The symbol text is Pandoc markdown, so `m^2^` renders as a superscript.
Some units have no space before them (`%`, `°`), and `pH` goes before the
number.

### Symbol or name

A unit prints in one of two **forms**: its symbol ("5 m") or its name ("five
metres"). By default the form follows the number: digits take the symbol,
and a spelled number takes the name.

```{r}
fmt_num(u(3, m))
fmt_word(u(3, m))
```

Three unit classes choose the form for one value: `.usym` the symbol,
`.uname` the name, `.nounit` no unit at all. In R code the same choice is the
`unit_form` argument:

```{r}
fmt_num(u(5, m), unit_form = "name")
fmt_num(u(1, m), unit_form = "name")
fmt_num(u(5, m), unit_form = "none")
fmt_num(u(12, NTU), unit_form = "name")
```

A name is singular only when its number prints as "1" or "one". The setting
`unit_form` (`auto`, `symbol` or `name`) in `_weft.yml`, or under a
document's `weft:` key, changes the default for a project or a document.

`fmt_unit()` prints the unit alone, for a table heading:

```{r}
fmt_unit(u(5, mg/L))
fmt_unit(u(5, mg/L), unit_form = "name")
```

### Converting as you print

The key `unit="m"` on a value or a span, and the argument `unit` in R code,
print the quantity in another unit. The number, the unit and the arm a span
chooses are all in that unit:

```{r}
fmt_num(u(150, cm), unit = "m")
```

A **ladder** is a list of units you accept, separated by `|`. weft prints
the quantity in the first unit that gives a number from 1 up to 1,000:

```{r}
fmt_num(u(2500, m), unit = "mm|m|km")
fmt_num(u(0.004, m), unit = "mm|m|km")
```

A vector takes one unit for all its numbers, the one where most of them
fit:

```{r}
fmt_num(u(c(0.4, 2500), m), unit = "mm|m|km")
```

Inside a pipe-table cell, write the ladder's bars as `\|`.

### Lists of quantities

A list prints the unit once, after the last item. `.pairs`, `.ul`, `.ol` and
`.dl` print it with each item.

```{r}
fmt_and(fmt_num(u(c(3, 5, 7), m)))
fmt_range(u(c(3, 5), m))
```

### Quantities that print as zero

A small quantity that prints as "0.0" records the same warned check as a
plain number, and the message suggests a prefixed unit where one would help:

```{r}
fmt_num(u(0.04, m))
```

## In a document

This document reads a project dictionary and a `units:` table, both shown
further down.

````{verbatim, lang = "markdown"}
---
title: "Units"
output: html_document
knitr:
  opts_knit:
    weft: !expr weft::weft_setup()
weft:
  dict_local:
    lab_sites:
      value: 4
      type: number
      definition: "Sites sent to the laboratory in this chapter."
      why: "Only the autumn survey sent samples away."
---

```{r data}
depth <- u(c(0.42, 0.65, 1.31), m)
visited <- u(12, sites)
core <- u(150, cm)
last_year <- 2024
```

The reach is `r dict$reach_len`{.num} long, or `r dict$reach_len`{unit="m"}.

Depths were `r depth`{.num .and}, a range of `r range(depth)`{.range}.

We visited `r visited`{.num}, and the cores were `r core`{.uname unit="m"} long.

[# core was | # cores were]{n="core" unit="m"} kept.

Turbidity above `r dict$trigger`{.num} is reported.

Salinity is logged to `r dict$salinity_res`{.uname}, or `r dict$salinity_res`{.uname sigfig="1"}.

Records start in `r dict$first_year`, and the logger ran for `r last_year - dict$first_year`{.word} years.

`r dict_local$lab_sites`{.word .cap} sites went to the laboratory.

The first depth was `r depth[1]`.
````

It renders as:

```text
The reach is 2 km long, or 2,000 m.

Depths were 0.4, 0.7 and 1.3 m, a range of 0.4–1.3 m.

We visited 12 sites, and the cores were 1.5 metres long.

1.5 m cores were kept.

Turbidity above 10 NTU is reported.

Salinity is logged to 0.0 practical salinity units, or 0.01 practical
salinity units.

Records start in 2014, and the logger ran for ten years.

Four sites went to the laboratory.

The first depth was 0.42.
```

and the knit ends with two warnings, which do not fail the render:

```{verbatim, lang = "text"}
weft: 2 warned check(s)
  units.Rmd:33  [printed as zero] `r dict$salinity_res`
      0.01 printed as 0.0: add sigfig to show it, or digits to confirm it
  units.Rmd:39  [unit warning] `r depth[1]`
      weft: `r depth[1]` is a quantity (0.42) and its unit is not printed. Add `{.num}` to print it with its unit, or `{.nounit}` to say the unit is not wanted (rule 4.4.10).
```

A bare value prints a quantity as knitr prints it, without the unit, and
weft warns because the reader loses the unit. Add `{.num}` to print it, or
`{.nounit}` to say you meant to drop it.

## Units weft does not know

weft starts from the units package's database, and adds a table of its own
for units common in environmental reports:

```{r}
unit_defaults()[, c("unit", "is", "name", "symbol", "before")]
```

A unit that neither knows is an error:

```{r, error = TRUE}
u(5, sites)
```

There are two ways to add one. A dictionary entry with that unit registers
it when the dictionary is read. The `units:` table in `_weft.yml` registers
it when the configuration is read, and gives it a name, a plural, a symbol,
or a definition. The document above used this `_weft.yml`:

```yaml
units:
  sites:
    name: site
    symbol: false
  PSU:
    name: practical salinity unit
```

`symbol: false` makes `sites` print by its name in every form ("12 sites").
The `PSU` row gives a name to a unit the default table already has, so
`.uname` can print it. Each row takes up to six fields:

| Field | Sets |
|---|---|
| `name` | the singular name |
| `plural` | the plural, when the English rule gets it wrong |
| `symbol` | the symbol text, or `false` for none |
| `space` | whether a space goes between the number and the symbol |
| `is` | what the unit is: `base`, a number, or an amount of another unit (`4.54609 L`) |
| `before` | `true` to write the unit before the number |

Some unit symbols mean something unexpected to the units package. weft
refuses those rather than print a wrong value:

```{r, error = TRUE}
u(5, mt)
```

weft keeps the units tables in R's user cache folder
(`tools::R_user_dir("weft", "cache")`) so that a new session starts faster.
`options(weft.units_cache = FALSE)` turns that off.

## The dictionary

The **dictionary** holds the values a project chose, as opposed to values
it computed. Each **entry** has a key, a `value`, a `type` and a
`definition`. It lives in `dict.yml` at the project root. This one has an
entry of every type:

```{r}
writeLines(c(
  "trigger:",
  "  value: 10",
  "  type: quantity",
  "  unit: NTU",
  "  term: turbidity trigger",
  "  definition: \"Turbidity above which a site is reported.\"",
  "reach_len:",
  "  value: 2000",
  "  type: quantity",
  "  unit: m",
  "  display: km",
  "  definition: \"Length of the surveyed reach.\"",
  "min_samples:",
  "  value: 5",
  "  type: number",
  "  definition: \"Fewest samples a site needs in a season.\"",
  "first_year:",
  "  value: 2014",
  "  type: year",
  "  definition: \"First year of the logger record.\"",
  "survey_start:",
  "  value: 2024-09-02",
  "  type: date",
  "  definition: \"First day of the spring survey.\"",
  "catchment:",
  "  value: \"Eastern catchment\"",
  "  type: string",
  "  definition: \"Name used for the study area.\"",
  "  avoid: [\"east catchment\"]",
  "tier_lab:",
  "  value: {ref: Reference, mod: Moderately disturbed, high: Highly disturbed}",
  "  type: labels",
  "  definition: \"Display names for the disturbance tiers.\"",
  "trend_word:",
  "  value:",
  "    - {below: 0.95, phrase: \"a fall in\"}",
  "    - {at_most: 1.05, phrase: \"no change in\"}",
  "    - {phrase: \"a rise in\"}",
  "  type: breaks",
  "  definition: \"Wording for this year's mean over last year's.\""
), "dict.yml")
```

| `type` | `value` | Read as |
|---|---|---|
| `number` | a number | a number |
| `quantity` | a number, with a `unit` | a quantity, in its `display` unit when it has one |
| `year` | a four-digit year | a year, which never gets a thousands mark |
| `date` | `YYYY-MM-DD` | a `Date` |
| `string` | text | a string |
| `labels` | a map from key to phrase | a `lookup()` function |
| `breaks` | a list of bands, each with `below` or `at_most` and a `phrase` | a `brk()` function |

In a knit, weft reads `dict.yml` itself and makes the object `dict`, so the
prose and the chunks read `dict$trigger`. At the console, `read_dict()`
reads it:

```{r}
dict <- read_dict("dict.yml")
dict
dict$reach_len
dict$first_year + 1
dict$tier_lab("mod")
dict$trend_word(1.02)
fmt_range(range(c(dict$first_year, dict$first_year + 10)))
```

`dict$key` matches the key exactly. A key that is not there is an error, never
`NULL`, and the dictionary cannot be changed from R:

```{r, error = TRUE}
dict$triger
dict$trigger <- 5
```

`read_dict()` checks every entry and reports every problem in the file at
once, each with its line:

```{r, error = TRUE}
writeLines(c(
  "depth:", "  value: 010", "  type: number", "  definition: Mean depth.",
  "spot:", "  value: 3", "  type: count", "  definition: A spot check."
), "bad.yml")
read_dict("bad.yml")
```

Besides the three required fields, an entry may have `unit` and `display`
(quantities only), `decision`, `term` and `avoid`. `decision` points at the
record of why the value was chosen, such as a GitHub issue number;
`verify()` checks that each pointer resolves. The setting `decisions` in
`_weft.yml` says where pointers resolve: `github` (the default),
`github:<owner>/<repo>`, a file pattern such as `decisions/{id}-*.md`, or a
function.

### A chapter's own values

A value that holds for one document only goes in that document's front
matter, under `weft:` and `dict_local:`, with a `why` that says why it is
not in the project dictionary. The document above has one. It is read as
`dict_local$key`, never `dict$key`, so a reader of the source sees at once
that the value is local.

### The glossary

`dict_glossary()` writes the dictionary as a Pandoc definition list. A chunk
that calls it is the glossary; it needs no `results: asis`:

```{r}
cat(dict_glossary(dict))
```

In a knit, `dict_glossary()` with no argument uses the knit's dictionary.

### Spellings to avoid

`avoid` lists spellings that should be the entry's `term`, or for a string
entry its value. `dict_vale()` writes them as a rule for the prose linter
[Vale](https://vale.sh). It says what it will write first:

```{r}
dict_vale(dict)
cat(readLines("styles/Weft/Terms.yml"), sep = "\n")
```

### Finding values to put in the dictionary

`dict_seed()` reads a project's documents, runs nothing, and lists names that
two or more documents assign a literal value to, as candidates for the
dictionary:

```{r}
writeLines(c("```{r}", "trigger <- 10", "n_sites <- 3", "```"), "spring.Rmd")
writeLines(c("```{r}", "trigger <- 10", "n_sites <- 4", "```"), "autumn.Rmd")
dict_seed(c("spring.Rmd", "autumn.Rmd"))[, c("name", "value", "differs", "n")]
```

`trigger` holds one value in both documents, so it is a stipulation that
belongs in `dict.yml`. `n_sites` differs, and the author decides what it is.

`use_dictionary()` writes a starter `dict.yml` and a schema that editors use
to check it as you type. See `vignette("setup", package = "weft")`.
